scenarios.title: Session chips with details shown
scenarios.caption: The same five sessions with 'Show session details in chips' enabled: each chip carries a secondary line under its title.

scenarios.title: Serial connect form
scenarios.caption: Serial launches ask only for a device path and line settings; there is no host/credential concept for a local serial device.

scenarios.title: SFTP connect form
scenarios.caption: The SFTP launch surface defaults to opening the graphical two-pane file manager once connected.

scenarios.title: SSH connect form with Advanced settings expanded

scenarios.title: SSH connect form
scenarios.caption: The default SSH launch surface: a Connection section led by the squashed user@host:port field and repeating it as Username, Host and Port, an Authentication section for the credential method, and the durable-remote-session toggle, with Advanced settings collapsed.

scenarios.title: Pinned pane details and unread member
scenarios.caption: The production group chip opens themed, keyboard-accessible member details with an unread build pane; no real sessions, secrets or user configuration.

scenarios.title: Equal 1:1 split
scenarios.caption: Two live terminal panes at equal width with the same content padding and one physical-pixel divider.

scenarios.title: Four live desktop panes
scenarios.caption: Production composition with controlled fake SSH surfaces; full-opacity siblings, focused inset and shared one-physical-pixel dividers. Not native qualification.

scenarios.title: Compact pane action menu
scenarios.caption: The hovered member menu keeps Move/Detach and guarded Close distinct from neighboring panes.

scenarios.title: Transient hover handle
scenarios.caption: A real top-edge pointer hover reveals only the compact grip/name/menu; terminal geometry and padding are unchanged.

scenarios.title: Equal-split hover details
scenarios.caption: Actual pointer-hover member details, not the pinned popup, over an equal split with an unread member.

scenarios.title: Three-pane hover details
scenarios.caption: Actual pointer-hover member details over two panes beside one, with focused and unread members distinguished.

scenarios.title: Unequal-split hover details
scenarios.caption: Actual pointer-hover member details over a 2:1 width split with an unread member.

scenarios.title: Pane configuration dialog
scenarios.caption: Compact production Pane Layout: selectable members, visual presets, rearrange/equalize/zoom, grouped actions and a separate guarded-close footer.

scenarios.title: Source-specific destination picker
scenarios.caption: Click-grip reveals an accessible target chooser, directional/Swap cross and separated source Detach/Close actions.

scenarios.title: Explicit pane rearrangement
scenarios.caption: Window-local manipulation mode shows all handles and Done without allocating a title row.

scenarios.title: Single terminal without a split
scenarios.caption: The production single-view terminal retains its normal content padding; controlled synthetic SSH session.

scenarios.title: Two panes beside one
scenarios.caption: Three live terminal panes: two stacked on the left beside one full-height pane on the right.

scenarios.title: Unequal 2:1 width split
scenarios.caption: Two live terminal panes with a 2:1 width ratio; padding is reserved inside each pane.

scenarios.title: Host access off
scenarios.caption: Production hosting controls with an absent synthetic host. Identity and creation controls remain hidden.

scenarios.title: Host access requested
scenarios.caption: Requested intent is not readiness. Synthetic account selection grants no host credentials or authority.

scenarios.title: Explicit account-scoped host discovery
scenarios.caption: Synthetic last-listed host metadata. Opening does not query the service or assert online availability.

scenarios.title: Host discovery with retained results
scenarios.caption: A synthetic explicit-discovery failure retains useful previous metadata; no native or real-service acceptance.

scenarios.title: Narrow host discovery
scenarios.caption: The same production host choices at 360 logical points, with synthetic account identity only.

scenarios.title: Offline host profile editor
scenarios.caption: Production editor with synthetic saved public host hints; no discovery or authentication.

scenarios.title: Narrow offline host profile editor
scenarios.caption: The production editor at 360 logical points; no native keyboard qualification.

scenarios.title: Session Inspector over a durable tmux session
scenarios.caption: The same overlay for a session attached through fesTerm's durable persistence provider, showing the extra 'Durable session' facts and 'Resume' (rather than 'Reconnect') action.

scenarios.title: Session Inspector over an SSH session
scenarios.caption: The inspector overlay reporting connection facts and a pending host-key fingerprint for a plain SSH shell, without covering the terminal it describes.

scenarios.title: Compare, after the file changed underneath the editor
scenarios.caption: The conflict banner stays pinned above a read-only, line-oriented comparison of the unsaved version against the one the file now holds, so the choice is made with both versions in sight.

scenarios.title: A document's three states side by side on the chips
scenarios.caption: Saved, edited, and changed-underneath are three different shapes before they are three different colours, so the row still reads with the colour taken away.

scenarios.title: Closing the last view of a document with unsaved changes
scenarios.caption: Closing the only remaining view of a typed-in document asks before anything is lost, names the file and where it lives, and makes Save the action the keyboard already has hold of.

scenarios.title: Find and Replace over the open document
scenarios.caption: One regular-expression dialect for the toolbar and the command area alike, saying which match of how many is current before anything is replaced.

scenarios.title: The per-view editor options
scenarios.caption: Line numbers, a fixed column count and vi keys belong to this view alone: another window on the same file keeps its own, and none of them touches the text.

scenarios.title: The editor with the Markdown outline beside it
scenarios.caption: The same rail the Markdown viewer has, offered while the file renders as Markdown: the headings stay in reach without scrolling to find out where you are.

scenarios.title: A Markdown file as it opens
scenarios.caption: A Markdown document lands in Preview, reading as the finished thing; the mode control above it is the way back to the source.

scenarios.title: Choosing where a document is written
scenarios.caption: One destination browser for both origins, stating an overwrite in words before the fact rather than asking a second time after the Save is already pressed.

scenarios.title: The native editor, everything saved
scenarios.caption: A fictional project's notes open for editing, with the origin, the commands, and the status band the editor reports through.

scenarios.title: The editor split with its live preview
scenarios.caption: One view, two panes: the text on the left and the same document rendered on the right, so a Markdown change can be read as it is typed.

scenarios.title: Source coloured by what it means
scenarios.caption: Keywords, strings, numbers, types and comments are told apart by role rather than by language, from the same palette the Markdown preview's fenced code uses.

scenarios.title: The native editor holding unsaved changes
scenarios.caption: The same document after typing: the banner, the chip state, and the status band all report one unsaved document rather than disagreeing.

scenarios.title: The vi command area over the open document
scenarios.caption: One line above the persistent status bar, never in place of it: what the document is and where the caret sits stay readable while a command is being typed.

scenarios.title: A view with vi compatibility switched on
scenarios.caption: The view says which mode it is in, in words, above the text as well as in the status bar, so a letter behaving as a command is never a surprise.

scenarios.title: A vi search matching as it is typed
scenarios.caption: The same regular-expression dialect the Find bar uses, counting what Enter is about to accept rather than what was last run.
